This is consistent with block dissipated-power(model power_gain) being too low for some block(s). Linear RC => S=dT/dP_cmd is constant. residual_s(workload)=sum_b S[s][b]*P_b*x_b, x_b=g_true/g_model-1. Plan: compute S via free finite-diff rc_runs (+1W each block from nominal r1), then fit x_b from measured residuals. Then verify by editing power_gain.

Per-sensor G-1 (avg nominal & 1.15x): c0 .064, c1 .124, c2 .066, c3 .085, c4 .030, c5 .054, c6 .096, c7 .115, pkg .161. At LOW power residuals ~0 (no offset) => multiplicative/gain, not additive. A model power/R error would make G distribution-DEPENDENT and NON-uniform; instead G is per-sensor and distribution-invariant => SENSOR slope (gain) faults. Model (v0) is essentially correct; keep it. c4 G-1=0.030 sits at the 3% spec ceiling => treat as healthy/within-spec. All other 8 exceed spec => gain faults. Commit: 8 instrument faults (slope, reads high by fraction of rise), model_problems empty.

Proof: per-sensor ratio K=(real-42)/(model-42) for right/cooler cores c4,c5,c6,c7 is DISTRIBUTION-DEPENDENT: c4 1.03(nominal)/1.12(left-heavy,cold)/0.97(right-heavy,hot); c7 1.11/1.21/1.04; c5,c6 similar. When a core is COLD it reads relatively HOTTER than model (receives heat reality doesn't route); when it is the HOT one it reads relatively COOLER (reality sheds heat it keeps). A fixed sensor gain CANNOT vary with load distribution. Min-power(m3)~0 and l3-max(m45)~0 consistent (small gradients). Magnitude ~8-10% of rise on cold cores => lateral conductance ~8% too low (model/reality-1 ~ -0.08). (B) SENSORS: c0,c1,c2,c3,pkg have STABLE ratios across ALL loads (c1 1.10-1.12 everywhere incl left/right-heavy; c0 1.05; pkg 1.17) => genuine SLOPE(gain) faults (fraction of rise): c0 .06, c1 .11, c2 .06, c3 .09, pkg .17. (c4 ~.03 within spec; c5,c6,c7 contaminated by model so reported magnitudes = nominal baseline .06/.10/.11). c4 excluded. Reporting: 8 sensor slope faults (c0,c1,c2,c3,c5,c6,c7,pkg) + 1 global lateral-conductance model problem.
152Propose h2Model v0 under-predicts lateral (inter-block) thermal conductance (heat spreading), so cooler blocks are predicted too cool and hotter blocks too warm. Manifest as load-distribution-dependent per-sensor ratios on c4-c7. Additionally several sensors have fixed slope(gain) errors (stable ratios across loads): c0,c1,c2,c3,pkg certain; c5,c6,c7 baseline gains.

At left-heavy load (m50-52) cold core c4 reads +1.8C above its gain-corrected model prediction while fitting exactly at nominal; a fixed sensor gain cannot vary with power distribution. There is a real model (lateral-spreading) error.

424Propose h3Reality is FLATTER and HOTTER than model v0: at nominal real core spread is only 3C (81,80,84,81,81,78,78,78) vs model spread 6.2C, and real average rise is ~6-7% higher. Model over-differentiates (keeps heat local) and is globally too cool. Signature of model under-predicting inter-block (lateral) heat spreading + a global under-prediction of temperature rise. Per-sensor apparent 'gains' are largely the spatial manifestation of this, not independent sensor slope faults, EXCEPT where a sensor stays off across loads.

575NoteCONVERGED DECOMPOSITION. Using ONLY workloads whose power maps I know exactly (nominal m1/r66; periph-min m44/r86; single-core-max), the balanced-load residuals correlate strongly with node coldness: model temp (nominal): pkg66.2, c7 74.1, c6 75.4, c1 75.9, c5 76.3, c3 78.1, c0 80.3, c4 80.3, c2 81.5 real-model resid: pkg+3.8, c7+3.9, c6+2.6, c1+4.1, c5+1.7, c3+2.9, c0+0.7, c4+0.7, c2+2.5 ratio (real-42)/(model-42): pkg1.16, c7 1.12, c6 1.08, c1 1.12, c5 1.05, c3 1.08, c0 1.02, c4 1.02, c2 1.06 => COLDER node => LARGER apparent gain. Exactly the signature of MODEL UNDER-PREDICTING lateral heat spreading (model keeps heat local: hot cores keep too much, cold bystanders/pkkg get too little). This explains "all sensors read high, more when cold" WITHOUT any sensor fault. This is why the pure-8-sensor-gain commit was rejected. Single-core-max confirms: c3 self at core3-max = 62.0 vs model 62.65 (ratio 0.97, exact); c7 at core7-max 59 vs 57.94 (1.13); c2 core2-max 62 vs 61.82 (1.0). Hot SOURCE reads ~exact -> no sensor gain; neighbors too warm. Real core spread at nominal ~6 C vs model spread ~7.4 C => model over-differentiates (flatter reality). Global: real mean rise ~36.6 vs model ~34.0 => model ~7% too cold die-wide as well (spreading alone cannot raise the mean; needs boundary term). Plan: fit boundary R factor (global) + lateral conductance factor (spreading) via free rc_runs at nominal + periph-min + core3-max.

654NoteQUANTITATIVE. Exact-power workloads only. Real per-sensor apparent gain (real-42)/(v0model-42): N(np): c0 1.063 c1 1.108 c2 1.060 c3 1.092 c4 1.037 c5 1.059 c6 1.100 c7 1.103 pkg 1.162 P: c0 1.040 c1 1.105 c2 1.048 c3 1.076 c4 1.031 c5 1.050 c6 1.078 c7 1.116 pkg 1.182 C3: c0 1.11 c1 1.096 c2 0.918 c3 0.968 c4 1.020 c5 1.00 c6 0.870 c7 1.25 pkg 1.02 N and P (both cores-on, peripherals differ 22W vs 2W) give STABLE per-sensor gains -> not a peripheral-power effect. KEY ORDERING: apparent gain rises monotonically as OWN nominal power FALLS: c4(8.5W)=1.03, c0(9.1)=1.05, c2(8.2)=1.05, c3(8.2)=1.08, c5(6.7)=1.05, c7(7.1)=1.11, c6(6.4)=1.09, c1(6.4)=1.11, pkg(low)=1.17. => Low own power -> high apparent gain. Exactly what MODEL UNDER-PREDICTING LATERAL HEAT SPREADING produces: nodes whose heat is dominated by neighbor leakage get the biggest boost; high-power nodes (own heat dominates) least. So nearly ALL structure = one model spreading error, NOT 8 sensor gains (explains why commit1 rejected). MEAN: real mean rise 37.32 vs v0 34.45 (model too COLD) and real spread (core max-min)=6.43 vs v0 7.35 (model too PEAKED). Two independent signatures: (a) global warmth deficit ~7.7% of rise; (b) under-spreading. Energy: more spreading LOWERS mean in this network (r84 b1 mean36.79 vs r90 b0.7 mean35.82 at same a), so spreading cannot supply the warmth -> global term genuinely separate. Fit targets: mean rise 37.32, core spread 6.43. Interp from a=1.1 data: b~0.80 (spread), then a~1.15 (mean). Running a=1.15,b=0.80.

717NoteDECISIVE ENERGY ARGUMENT (rules out single-fault explanations): Real device vs v0 at nominal: real core MEAN rise 38.46, v0 35.73 (real +7.6% hotter); real core SPREAD 6.43, v0 7.35 (real FLATTER). In this RC network, increasing lateral spreading conductance LOWERS the mean (r67 showed more lateral -> cooler) while it reduces spread. So NO single conductance change gives mean-UP + spread-DOWN. Two independent effects required: (1) BOUNDARY conductance too HIGH in model -> model over-cools die-wide -> model too cold. Fix = raise boundary R. a~1.15. (2) LATERAL conductance too LOW in model -> model keeps heat local (too peaked). Fix = lower lateral R. b~0.8. Two-param fit (boundary x1.15, all lateral x0.8) => r93: mean rise 38.57, spread 6.48 vs real 38.46, 6.43. Aggregate match excellent. Verified on periph-min (r94) and core3-max (r95): gross structure now correct (v0 had +2..+4 at nominal, now mostly <1.1, and residual is at measurement noise level on single reads). Sensor faults RULED OUT: c4,c5,pkg high residuals VANISH at low-power / core3-max loads (c4 resid +0.16 at core3max, pkg +0.18) -> load-dependent -> model, NOT instrument. No stuck, no excess noise (repeats scatter<=1), no constant offset (m3 ~0). NOT power_gain: 4% power tolerance <0.7C (Jacobian 1.3-1.5C/W); can't make 7.6% mean. Magnitudes for report (conductance, larger=more): lateral model/reality-1 = -0.20 (model 20% low); boundary model/reality-1 = +0.15 (model 15% high). Card left at a=1.15,b=0.8.
718Propose h4Two independent GLOBAL model thermal-conductance errors, no sensor faults. (A) Lateral/inter-block thermal conductance too LOW (model under-spreads: keeps heat local, too peaked) — model/reality-1 = -0.20. (B) Boundary die-to-ambient conductance too HIGH (model over-cools, too cold die-wide) — model/reality-1 = +0.15. Proven by energy constraint: real is BOTH hotter (mean rise +7.6%) and flatter (spread 6.43 vs 7.35), which no single conductance change in this network can produce. Sensor faults excluded: all high per-sensor residuals vanish at low-power/core3-max loads (load-dependent => model).

Cannot flatten. - lateral conductance only: aligning temps flattens (spread down) but lowers mean (r90 x0.7 gave mean 35.82). Cannot raise mean. Real is BOTH hotter (mean +7.6%) AND flatter (spread 6.43 vs 7.35) => needs boundary conductance DOWN (real warmer die-wide) + lateral conductance UP (real more spread). Two independent global faults. MAGNITUDES (model/reality-1, conductance, larger=more): - boundary die-to-ambient conductance: model too HIGH. R_correct=1.15*R_v0 => g_real=g0/1.15 => g_model/g_real-1=+0.15. - lateral/inter-block conductance: model too LOW. R_correct=0.8*R_v0 => g_real=1.25 g0 => g_model/g_real-1=-0.20. INSTRUMENT: NO faults. Self-heat exact (m53 c3 self 62 vs model 62.06; m34/35 c2 exact) rules out gain faults; repeats scatter<=1 (no noise fault); m3 min-power ~0 (no offset); not stuck. All nominal +2..+4 residuals are the model spreading/boundary errors (load-dependent, vanish on self-heat). COMMITTING: 2 model problems (global), 0 instrument, 0 undetermined.

Laterals = v0*0.810. Verticals=v0, v_core4=1.9065. power_gain=v0 (core4 0.961237). KEY REFRAME: self-heat dT/dP_self (model/real) at single-core-max: c0 1.033, c3 1.028, c6 1.004, c7 0.979, c4 1.189. So c0/c3/c6/c7 self EXACT (within gap) -> NO boundary/power/vertical global error affects them, and NO sensor gain on those (hot source reads exact). c4 is the SINGLE outlier (19% too much self-heat = power_gain.core4 too high). c4 halo test with power_gain.core4=0.85 earlier (r199-201) matched core4max (c4 59.74 vs 59.5, c2 53.91 vs 54) AND rightheavy (c4 73.0 vs 73.0) BEAUTIFULLY. => power_gain.core4 too high (~0.85-0.86 real vs 0.961 model). But balanced loads still show real +2-3 hotter than model everywhere. Self-heat exact but balanced hot => the extra heat comes from PERIPHERY blocks (io/mc/uncore/misc/l3) which are at MIN during single-core tests. At nominal they add ~17.5W. Model under-predicts periphery->core coupling OR periphery power. Observation_map: dot(row,P_diss) != temp rise (gives 0.28 vs real ~38), row sums ~0 -> it's a CENTERED/contrast basis, useless for magnitude. Ignore. NEXT: test raising power_gain.core4 to fit; separately test periphery coupling/power. But self-heat exact for c0,c3,c6,c7 constrains b+v globally.

1869NoteFRESH v0 (r251=80.291 exact). Real data (exact power maps) vs v0 preds: BASELINE m54 real 47,46,46,46,46,45,46,46 |pkg46 ; v0 r254 45.83,45.39,45.95,45.61,45.83,45.43,45.34,45.21 |44.42 core0max m55 66,53,55,51,52,50,50,48 |50 ; v0 r252 65.47,51.78,53.79,49.48,50.63,48.62,48.78,48.03 |47.95 core3max m53 51,53,50,62,50,52,48,51 |50 ; v0 r255 49.50,51.45,50.12,62.06,49.26,51.39,48.30,48.62 |49.22 core4max m56/59 51,48.5,53.5,50,59.5,49,50.5,49 |47.5 ; v0 r253 50.32,48.48,54.72,48.88,62.48,49.07,51.92,49.02 |47.73 core6max m60 49,49,50,49,54,48,58,50 |48 ; v0 r256 48.15,47.20,49.24,47.67,52.26,48.01,57.39,48.82 |46.64 core7max m57 49,49,50,49,50,52,50,59 |48 ; v0 r257 47.85,47.47,48.47,48.60,48.82,51.61,48.91,57.94 |47.42 NOMINAL real avg(m1,6,13,38-41) 82.71,79.57,83.86,81.43,81.71,78.29,78.71,77.43 |70.14 ; v0 r251 80.29,75.91,81.48,78.12,80.30,76.27,75.37,74.13 |66.21 SELF-heat ratios (model rise/real rise): c0 1.034,c3 1.028,c6 1.004,c7 0.979, c4 1.233 (OUTLIER), all others within 3% spec. c4 core4max: self model 62.48 vs real 59.5 -> model +2.98 too hot; NEIGHBORS c2 -1.22, c6 -1.42 also model-too-hot; pkg -0.23 (matches!). So c4 excess is LOCAL to c4 cluster, package unaffected => NOT extra total heat, it's redistribution/trapping at c4. Nominal: all sensors +2 to +4 too cold (model) EXCEPT c4 +1.41 (relatively model-too-hot). Global warmth real>model grows with power. DECISION: c4-local model fault + global warmth. Testing c4 mechanism now.
1870Propose h5c4 has a LOCALIZED model fault: at core4max the model over-predicts c4 self-heat by 23% (62.48 vs real 59.5) and its silicon neighbors c2,c6 are also model-too-hot, while T_package matches. Under-spreading (weak lateral) would make neighbors model-too-COLD; observed is model-too-HOT, so heat is over-produced/over-retained at the c4 silicon. Candidate mechanisms: power_gain.core4 too high (extra heat) vs v_core4/b_core4 (heat-escape) resistance too high. Test by editing each and comparing core4max.
1871Propose h6Global model under-predicts temperature when multiple cores are hot simultaneously: at nominal (all cores ~nominal power) every sensor reads +2 to +4C above model, but at single-core-max self-heat is exact. m44 (cores nominal, periphery min) still shows +1.6..+3.7, so it is core-core driven, not peripheral. This is a separate global model error (boundary/lateral conductance) beyond the c4-local fault.

1882Notec4 has TWO contradictory signatures: - core4max (c4 hot source): model c4 +2.98 TOO HOT, neighbors c2/c6 also model-too-hot, pkg matches -> consistent with c4 dissipating LESS power in reality (power_gain.core4 too high). - nominal (c4 bystander among hot cores): model c4 +1.41 TOO COLD (like everything at nominal -> global model-too-cold). power_gain.core4=0.85: core4max GREAT (c4 60.4 vs 59.5, c2 53.6 vs 53.5, c6 51.1 vs 50.5) BUT nominal c4 78.92 vs 81.71 (too cold). So power_gain fix works LOCALLY but global-cold dominates nominal. HYPOTHESIS: TWO faults — (local) power_gain.core4 too high, (global) something makes model too cold when many blocks hot. Doing Jacobian finite-diff (13 free runs +2W each block) then least-squares fit residual = J·δP_b + sensor offsets across 7 loads.

1896NoteMODEL Jacobian (per-W, baseline r254->each column r262-r274), and REAL Jacobian from single-core-max columns (real ΔT/ΔP from m54 baseline). KEY RATIO real/model for CORE self & coupling: Core SELF-heat ratios (real/model): c0 0.968, c3 0.973, c6 0.996, c7 1.021, c4 0.810 <-- c4 model self 23% TOO HIGH. c4 column off-diagonals (real/model): c0 .889, c1 .811, c2 .855, c5 1.098(small), c6 .684, c7 .790, pkg .453(small). => WHOLE c4 column ~0.81-0.89 (model uniformly too big). Uniform scale of self+couplings = c4 HEAT MAGNITUDE too big => power_gain.core4 too high (~true gain 0.78 vs model 0.961). NOT lateral/v_core4 (those predict wrong coupling sign). Other core columns off-diagonal (real/model): mostly >1 (core0:c3 1.29,c4 1.25,c5 1.57; core6:c1 1.66,c3 1.46,c4 1.24; core7:c2 1.59,c1 1.44,c4 1.34). => model UNDER-predicts lateral coupling; but self ~exact (vertical path correct). Signature = LATERAL conductance too LOW in model. => At nominal (many cores hot) missing lateral coupling => model too cold everywhere (+2.7). At single-core, source self exact but neighbors model-too-cold (+1.2). CONSISTENT with lateral-too-low. So working mechanism: (A) power_gain.core4 too HIGH (~0.78 true) -- LOCAL fault. (B) lateral conductance too LOW (model under-spreads) -- global. Possibly (C) boundary too high needed to raise MEAN at nominal (lateral alone can't raise mean by energy conservation) -- BUT boundary-up breaks self-exactness unless paired with lateral-up. h4 (boundary x1.15 + lateral x0.8) fit nominal but MISSED c4 => likely why commit failed. TEST NOW: set power_gain.core4=0.78, run core4max + nominal + core0max. Then add lateral/boundary and iterate to match ALL loads within gap 0.61.

2115NoteBOUNDARY SCALE SWEEP (peripheral boundary R, v0 base). Real core-readings vs model, and pkg: ×1.4 (r339-348): cores fit within ~±1 (nominal resid -.14,+.36,+.63,+.38,+.75,-.82,+1.12,+.26), pkg +1.37 COLD (68.77 vs 70.14 nominal). m44 cores +0.1..+1.4 fit. ×1.5 (r355-357): cores run -1.3 HOT at nominal (84.17..|69.91 vs 82.71..|70.14), pkg -0.23 (69.91 ~ real 70.14, matches!). m44 cores -1.3..-2.4 hot. Sensitivity: going 1.4->1.5, pkg warms +1.14, cores warm +1.6. Cores MORE sensitive than pkg (~1.4x). So NO single peripheral-boundary scale zeroes both: cores want ~1.42, pkg wants ~1.52. NOT lateral (lateral-up would raise neighbors at c4max, but real neighbors COOLER than model).\n\nNOMINAL residual (real-model): +2.42,+3.66,+2.38,+3.31,+1.41,+2.02,+3.34,+3.30,+3.93. (b) GLOBAL boundary conductance DOWN (raise boundary R) - dies-wide warmth. (c) power_gain.core4 DOWN - c4 local. 2452NoteFINAL MODEL (v1860): boundary R×1.15 + all 46 laterals R×0.80 + power_gain.core4=0.82. Verified NOT unilateral: - LATERAL-ALONE (r414: pkg 65.53 vs real 70.14, +4.6 cold) => cannot raise mean (energy conservation). Boundary genuinely needed. - BOUNDARY-ALONE flattens partly but leaves core residuals ~-1 to -1.5 (too cold). - 3-param gives best fit: nominal r428 cores within ~1, pkg +1.18; uniform r429; m44 r430; single-core-max r411-413 c4 59.29 vs 59.5 exact. \nREPORTED MAGNITUDES (model_original/reality-1, the ERROR): 1. boundary conductance (die-wide→ambient): R_correct=1.15*R_v0 => g_real=g_v0/1.15 => model/reality-1=+0.15. location global. 2. lateral inter-block conductance: R_correct=0.80*R_v0 => g_real=1.25*g_v0 => model/reality-1=-0.20. location global. 3. power_gain.core4: model 0.961237, reality~0.82 => model/reality-1=+0.172. location core4. \nINSTRUMENT: NONE. Evidence: c0,c1,c2,c3,c6,c7 all read EXACT when they are the self-heated source at single-core-max (c3 62.0 vs model 62.06; c1 58 vs 57.92) -> no core sensor gain faults (a gain would inflate self-heat reading). Repeats scatter<=1 (no excess noise). Min-power residual~0 (no offset). c4 anomaly is load-DEPENDENT (model-hot as source, model-cold as bystander) -> MODEL lateral/power, NOT sensor. pkg-cold grows with peripheral heat (m44 +0.49 vs nominal +1.18) -> peripheral-path MODEL error, not pkg sensor gain. \nUNDETERMINED: none (all anomalies attributed to the 3 model problems).

2931NoteFINAL COMMIT DECISION (3 model problems, 0 instrument, 0 undetermined):\n1) Boundary die→ambient conductance too HIGH in model (model over-cools die-wide; real hotter). Card R×1.15 => model/reality-1 = +0.15. location global.\n2) Lateral inter-block conductance too LOW in model (model keeps heat local, too peaked; real flatter). Card R×0.8 => model/reality-1 = -0.20. location global.\n3) power_gain.core4 too HIGH (model over-computes c4 self-heat +23%). model 0.961 vs real 0.78 => model/reality-1 = +0.23. location core4, quantity = core4 commanded-to-dissipated power gain.\nEnergy argument is the basis: real is BOTH hotter (mean rise 38.46 vs 35.73) AND flatter (spread 6.43 vs 7.35); lateral-up flattens but lowers mean, boundary-down raises mean; both needed. c4 isolated by self-heat.\nSensors: no fault. Self-heat reads exact for c0,c2,c3,c6,c7 as source (a gain would inflate the hot-source reading). Repeats scatter<=1 (no excess noise). Min-power residual~0 (no offset). The apparent per-sensor 'gains' are the spatial manifest of the model spreading/boundary errors (load-dependent).

3206NoteBREAKTHROUGH — clean single-source residuals vs v0 (exact maps r359-363,r540,r539):\nsource self-residual (real-v0): c0 +0.53, c3 -0.06, c4 -2.98(model HOT), c6 +0.61, c7 +1.06, c1 +2.08.\nPeriphery-at-min loads (baseline,leftheavy,all single-core) fit v0 within boundary-warmth ~+0.6. At ~15W single-core, model boundary over-cool gives ~+0.6 uniform. Subtract it:\nc1 +2.08-0.6=+1.48 on rise14 = 10% -> GENUINE c1 SENSOR GAIN\nc6 +0.61-0.6=0 (healthy), c7 +1.06-0.6=+0.46/13=3.5% (borderline, ~spec), c0,c3 healthy.\nc4 -2.98 => power_gain.core4 model too high.\n\nTWO-GLOBAL fit validated: boundary×1.15 + lateral×0.8 reproduces nominal mean-rise 38.57 vs real 38.46, spread 6.48 vs 6.43 (near-perfect). Lateral alone cools mean (r548 mean~34), boundary alone can't flatten. Energy requires BOTH.\n\nFINAL ANSWER:\nMODEL (3): (1) boundary conductance too high +0.15 (R×1.15); (2) lateral conductance too low -0.20 (R×0.8); (3) power_gain.core4 too high, model 0.961 vs real 0.78 => +0.23.\nINSTRUMENT (1): T_core1 slope gain, reads high ~+0.15 of rise above ambient (source residual +2.44 at core1max on rise 15.6).\nCard set: boundary×1.15, lateral×0.8, pg_core4=0.78 (v2466).
